turns.answer:
Done. Here's what I built and what I verified:

## What's in the project

**`src/scene.js`** — exports `createScene(THREE)` returning `{ scene, camera, update }`, building the scene with no renderer and no DOM access:
- **Ground plane** plus a **street grid of 99 buildings**, each with its own height drawn from 99 distinct values (9.6–74.5 units), every mesh tagged `userData.kind = "building"` (also `ground: 1`, `beacon: 5`)
- **Lit windows**: 396 emissive window meshes (the glowing-window meshes) over the buildings, so scattered windows glow amber/warm against the dark facades
- **11 lights**: a `HemisphereLight` (faint night sky), a `DirectionalLight` moon, and 9 `PointLight` street lamps; plus fog
- **`update(seconds)`** orbits the camera slowly around the city (it moves 47.7 units between t=0 and t=5) and keeps its look-target on the city center (cos angle 0.9999), still moving after t=5

**`index.html`** — full-window canvas, import map mapping `"three"` → `./vendor/three/three.module.min.js` (vendored r182, which resolves its own `three.core.min.js`), a `WebGLRenderer` with soft shadows and filmic tone mapping, a window-resize handler, and a `requestAnimationFrame` loop driving `update` from a clock.

## Verification results

1. **Node scene check** (`tools/check-scene.mjs`): *ALL CHECKS PASSED* — confirmed no renderer/DOM creation, all building tags, height variety, lights (incl. directional), fog, camera motion between t=0 and t=5 while looking at the city.
2. **Real browser run** (harness-driven headless Chrome over CDP): page loaded at `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` with readyState `complete`, canvas 1440×813, **0 JS exceptions**, and exactly 4 requests, all OK (`/`, `/src/scene.js`, both three.js modules) — only benign ReadPixels performance warnings from screenshotting.
3. **Night-scene screenshot analysis** (pure-stdlib PNG decoder, two frames 1.6 s apart): mean luminance **18.5 / 21.0** (< 70), **90 % of pixels dark**, sky darker than the city (11.1 vs 21.5), **4.8–6.5 % bright glowing pixels** (windows), and mean frame difference **26.0** (> 0.5, confirming the camera animates). All four night checks pass.

**Limits:** browser verification ran on software WebGL (SwiftShader), not a hardware GPU, so the screenshots prove correctness of the scene and animation rather than final frame rate on a real GPU. Helper scripts live in `tools/` and screenshots in `tools/shots/`.

turns.prompt:
Build a night city scene with three.js in this project. three.js is already here at
vendor/three/three.module.min.js (import it as "three" through an import map; there is no network,
so use only files in this project).

1. `src/scene.js` exports `createScene(THREE)` returning `{ scene, camera, update }`:
   - a ground plane and at least 40 buildings of varied heights (at least 8 different heights)
     laid out on a street grid; give every building mesh `userData.kind = "building"`
     (an InstancedMesh with that tag counts each instance);
   - lit windows: building materials (or separate window meshes) with an emissive color or an
     emissive map, so some windows glow;
   - at least two lights, one of them a directional, point or spot light (the moon or street
     lights), and fog;
   - `update(seconds)` moves the camera slowly around the city (it must move between t=0 and t=5)
     and keeps it looking at the city.
   `createScene` must not create a renderer or touch the DOM: it only builds the scene.
2. `index.html` shows the scene full-window: a WebGLRenderer, resizing with the window, and an
   animation loop that calls `update`. It must load and run without errors in the browser.

The scene should read as night: mostly dark, with glowing windows. Check your work as far as you
can, then tell me what you built.
turns.answer:
Everything checks out. Here's what I built and how it verifies:

## What was built

**`src/scene.js`** — exports `createScene(THREE)` returning `{ scene, camera, update }`. It builds only scene data: no renderer, no DOM calls (every texture is a `THREE.DataTexture` from typed arrays, so the module also runs in plain Node — which is how I tested it).

- **Ground + buildings**: a large dark ground plane (`userData.kind = "ground"`) plus **49 buildings on a 7×7 street-grid** (block pitch 18, grid spans 144×144 with a road cross every block), every one tagged `userData.kind = "building"` (`src/scene.js:253`). Heights use 9 tiers from 9 to 76 units with per-building jitter — the test found **25 distinct heights**; downtown blocks are taller by ring distance.
- **Lit windows**: procedurally generated facade textures pair a `map` with an `emissiveMap` of randomly lit window cells; materials use `emissive: 0xffffff, emissiveIntensity: 1.6` (`src/scene.js:241-242`). Stochastic per-building texture clones give varied window patterns; **105 meshes** end up with glowing emissive materials. Street lamps add `emissive: 0xffb663, intensity 3.2` (`:271`) with small halo quads.
- **Lights + fog**: **10 lights** — a `DirectionalLight` moon `0x9db8ff` (`:381`), **8 point lights** for street intersections `0xffa857` (`:317`), and a hemisphere fill — plus `FogExp2(0x070a16, 0.0058)` (`:405`); scene background `0x04060e`.
- **`update(seconds)`**: orbits the camera — `angle = 0.9 + seconds × 0.12`, radius 134, height 44 + gentle bob — and calls `lookAt(0, 14, 0)` every frame, so it always faces the city. Full lap ≈ 52 s (slow), and it clearly moves between t=0 and t=5.

**`index.html`** — import map mapping `"three"` → `./vendor/three/three.module.min.js` (`index.html:15-17`); a full-bleed `WebGLRenderer` with shadows and ACES tone mapping (`:27-34`); a `resize` handler on window resize (`:36-42`); and `renderer.setAnimationLoop` calling `update(clock.getElapsedTime())` then `render` (`:44-48`).

## Verification

**Node structural test** (against the current files) — all 11 checks pass:
- 49 buildings, all tagged; 25 distinct heights (≥ 8); ground present
- 10 lights (8 point + 1 directional + 1 hemisphere); fog present; 105 emissive meshes
- Camera moved **79.32 units between update(0) and update(5)**; look-at direction dot product toward city center = **0.9996** at both t=0 and t=5
- createScene ran fine in plain Node → proves no renderer/DOM usage

**Headless Chromium** (no network; served from the project): all four resources returned 200 (`index.html`, `src/scene.js`, `three.module.min.js`, `three.core.min.js` — only `/favicon.ico` 404, harmless), **zero console/JS errors**, exit 0. Two screenshots taken at ≈t 6 s and ≈t 15 s (saved in `/tmp/verify/night_city*.png`): both **~90 % dark pixels, mean luminance ≈ 15/255**, ~5.6 % bright pixels that are mixed warm (window/street amber) and cool (moon-blue), with the skyline/window pattern visibly shifted between the two shots — confirming the night look *and* that `update` moves the camera in the browser.

One trade-off: browser shots were software-rendered (SwiftShader), so they're slightly noisier than a real GPU, but layout, lighting, and motion are all faithfully captured.
